refutation_headline.description: PER-PAIR check: for each (E1, E2) ground-truth FALSE pair where E1 has a finite term model M, enumerate assignments of E2.lhs ∪ E2.rhs variables to elements of M; evaluate both sides in M's operation table; report refuted iff at least one assignment evaluates the sides to different model elements. NOT a per-E1 assumption — each individual pair is checked. 100% refutation across the checked pairs is therefore an EMPIRICAL result, not a construction-time guarantee: small term models in principle could satisfy accidental equations beyond E1's theory and thus fail to refute some FALSE consequents. The data says that did not happen for these 130 E1s — their small term models are equationally faithful, an interesting fact about strong/collapsing equations in the corpus.
